Named as successor in northern Kerala.

capitals.name: Mahodayapuram (Makotai, Kodungallur)
capitals.note: Infobox: "Mahodayapuram, or Makotai - the capital of the Cheraman Perumals" (present-day Kodungallur). Tradition says the last ruler "shifted his capital from Mahodayapuram (Kodungallur) to Kollam" without a date; Kollam was a second headquarters to c. 1122/23 (Rama Kulasekhara page).

correction.text: the region extending from the Palakkad Gap to Vembanad Lake

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no medieval Chera row). The page: "The Chera Perumal held outright authority over the region extending from the Palakkad Gap to Vembanad Lake." Infobox dates "c. 844 CE-c. 1124 CE" (earliest recorded c. 844-870); no area given. Sthanu Ravi "notably assisted the Cholas in conquering the western Tamil country" in the late 9th century.

correction.text: Kerala up to the Chandragiri river in the north and Nagercoil in the south

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "later extended up to the Chandragiri river in northern Kerala and to Nagercoil in the south" (undated); "Kolathu-nadu (in northern Kerala) came under the influence of the Chera Perumals only during the 11th century CE". From the early 11th century the kingdom was "attacked and eventually forced into submission by the Cholas"; the Chola dossier carries the overlordship. The page gives no area.

ledger.note: c. 844: the earliest recorded Chera Perumal reigns begin at Mahodayapuram. Infobox "c. 844 CE-c. 1124 CE" with spans "c. 844-870 (earliest recorded)", "c. 905-943", "962-1021" and "c. 1089-1124 (last)". The page names no founder.

11th century (bridge 1001): northern Kerala comes under Chera influence. "Kolathu-nadu (in northern Kerala) came under the influence of the Chera Perumals only during the 11th century CE"; the page gives no year.

region.text: Kollam and the country south to Nagercoil

ledger.note: c. 1097: Chola forces reach Kollam. They "advanced northwards from the south (Nagercoil) as far as the port of Kollam around 1097 AD", "probably led by" the general Kalinga Rayan. Earlier, "Between 1077 and 1081 AD, the Chola ruler Kulottunga I (1070-1120) conducted a campaign."

region.text: Kollam and the country south to Nagercoil

ledger.note: 1102: Kollam is recovered. "by 1102 AD Rama Kulasekhara appears to have recovered Kollam", so the Chola advance was short-lived.
c. 1124: the kingdom breaks up. "In the early 12th century, the medieval Chera kingdom of Kerala dissolved into several local powers"; Kolathunadu goes with the north.

region.text: Kerala up to the Chandragiri river in the north and Nagercoil in the south

ledger.note: c. 1124: the Chera Perumal kingdom dissolves. Infobox end c. 1124; a 1126 Cholapuram inscription calls Vira Kerala "the first independent ruler of Venadu". Venad, Kolathunadu and the future rulers of Kozhikode and Kochi are the successors; the last Perumal "disappeared from the Kerala 'mysteriously'" after dividing the kingdom, in tradition.

wars.name: Chola subjugation of the Chera Perumals
wars.outcome: "The Chera kingdom was attacked and eventually forced into submission by the Cholas in c. early 11th century CE"; "The Chera state in Kerala was subjugated during the reign of the Chola emperor Rajaraja I" (died 1014 per the Rajaraja I page) and Chola authority was "firmly established" under Rajendra I; the Cheras stayed as a Chola dependency.
wars.note: No year on the page; the span is "early 11th century" to the end of Rajaraja I's reign. The Rajaraja I page dates a Kandalur Salai triumph "around 988" but does not name the Cheras.

wars.name: Chola campaign to Kollam

zones.text: Kollam and the country south to Nagercoil

wars.outcome: Chola forces advanced from Nagercoil to Kollam around 1097; by 1102 Rama Kulasekhara "appears to have recovered Kollam".

certainty.note: No frontier is given on any page; the Palakkad Gap and Vembanad Lake mark the core, the rest is approximate.

notes: Cliopatria has no medieval Chera row. Two pages only; the first gives no regnal years and no war dates, so the dated events are the Chola advance of 1097-1102 and the infobox span. Dates 844 and 1124 are the infobox's 'c.'; the page does not give c. 800 or 1102. Chola overlordship from the early 11th century is recorded in the chola-empire dossier (vassal_start counterpart chera-perumal-kingdom). The 1001 'bridge' years are conventions for '11th century'. Successors venad, kolathunadu, kozhikode need dossiers (Cliopatria has none of the Kerala polities of the era). Gazetteer lacks Kodungallur, Palakkad, Chandragiri River.
